implemented_requirements.evidence: DIFFICULTIES dict in game.py defines (9,9,10), (16,16,40), (30,16,99) and gui.py creates an OptionMenu from DIFFICULTIES keys.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGUI.on_left_click binds <Button-1> to board.reveal(*pos) in gui.py.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.place_mines computes cell.adjacent; gui.draw renders the number with canvas.create_text using cell.adjacent.

implemented_requirements.requirement: If a mine is uncovered, the player loses
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.reveal sets game_over=True when cell.mine is True and reveals all mines; gui.draw shows "GAME OVER" when board.game_over and not board.won.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board updates visually after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: After reveal or flag toggle, gui.draw() is called to redraw the entire canvas.
MinesweeperGUI.on_right_click calls board.toggle_flag(*pos); Board.toggle_flag flips cell.flagged.
gui.draw_flag draws a red flag polygon when cell.flagged; draw() calls draw_flag for flagged cells.

judge.summary: The submitted code provides a complete, functional Minesweeper implementation with three difficulty levels, left‑click reveal, right‑click flagging, numeric hints, loss detection, win detection, and distinct flag graphics. The GUI is built with tkinter and appears ready to run, meeting all core requirements.
